summary: Defines a portion of the Management Information Base for managing the Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP). It was later replaced by RFC 5519.

eli5.summary: IGMP is how computers say they want to join a group broadcast. This lets management tools see and control that.

subtitle: Management tools for controlling group membership announcements

tldr.problem: Network administrators need a standard way to monitor and manage the Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) on their routers and hosts.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines a Management Information Base (MIB) with two tables: one tracking IGMP configuration and status per interface, and one tracking multicast group memberships per interface.
tldr.outcome: Administrators can use SNMP to read IGMP state and configure parameters like query intervals and robustness variables. RFC 5519 later updated this for IPv6.

today: RFC 2933 is a Proposed Standard for IGMP management. It was replaced by RFC 5519, which extended the MIB to cover IGMP version 3 and IPv6 multicast listener discovery.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
This RFC defines a Management Information Base (MIB) for managing the Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) version 1 and version 2 on IPv4 networks. A MIB is a structured database of objects that network management tools can query and modify using SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol). The MIB applies to both hosts and routers, though some objects are specific to routers.

IGMP is the protocol hosts use to announce they want to receive multicast traffic for a particular group address, and the protocol routers use to learn which groups have listeners on each interface.
sections.eli5: Network managers need a standard way to check which groups are active on a network and tune how IGMP works.

sections.title: IGMP and Network Management
sections.content:
IGMP allows hosts to join and leave IP multicast groups. Routers running IGMP learn which groups have active listeners on each interface and forward multicast packets only to interfaces with members. The protocol exists in two main versions: IGMP version 1 is simple but does not allow hosts to leave groups quickly; IGMP version 2 adds mechanisms for hosts to announce they are leaving a group immediately.

Before this MIB was defined, there was no standard way for administrators to monitor IGMP activity or configure protocol parameters on routers and hosts. This MIB fills that gap by exposing IGMP state to SNMP management stations.
sections.eli5: IGMP is how computers tell the network they want a broadcast. Managers need tools to watch this and adjust it.

sections.title: MIB Structure: Two Tables
sections.content:
The MIB consists of two main tables. The IGMP Interface Table contains one row for each interface on which IGMP is enabled. Each row tracks the IGMP version running on that interface, the IP address of the current IGMP querier (the router that sends membership queries), query timing parameters, statistics on membership joins and wrong-version queries, and timers. Key configurable parameters include igmpInterfaceQueryInterval (how often queries are sent, default 125 seconds) and igmpInterfaceRobustness (tuning for packet loss).

The IGMP Cache Table contains one row for each multicast group with members on a particular interface. Each row records whether the local system is a member of the group, the IP address of the host that last reported membership, how long the entry has existed, and how long before the membership will be aged out.
sections.eli5: One table lists active settings on each network interface. Another lists which broadcast groups have listeners.

sections.title: Configurable Objects and Version Support
sections.content:
The MIB allows administrators to configure IGMP behavior. The igmpInterfaceStatus object can be set to enable or disable IGMP on an interface. The igmpInterfaceVersion object can be set to run IGMP version 1 or version 2 (default is version 2). The igmpInterfaceQueryMaxResponseTime sets the maximum time hosts have to respond to membership queries (in tenths of seconds, default 100). The igmpInterfaceLastMembQueryIntvl controls leave latency by tuning the interval of group-specific queries.

Read-only query objects track the current querier's IP address, how long it has been the querier, when it will stop being querier, and statistics on received queries with incorrect versions and group membership joins on the interface.
sections.eli5: Managers can turn IGMP on or off, pick which version to use, and adjust timing to suit network conditions.

sections.title: Security and Access Control
sections.content:
Some MIB objects expose sensitive information. The igmpCacheSelf and igmpCacheLastReporter objects can be used to identify which machines are listening to a multicast group. Read-write and read-create objects allow administrators to configure IGMP, potentially causing denial of service if changed without authorization.

SNMPv1 provides no security; anyone on the network can read and modify these objects. The RFC recommends using SNMPv3 with the User-based Security Model and View-based Access Control, so that only authorized users can access or modify IGMP configuration. Administrators must properly configure their SNMP implementation to restrict access to IGMP objects.
sections.eli5: Seeing which computers are in a group could reveal private information. Only trusted managers should be able to change settings.
